title: Card Grading Prices (2026)
verdict: Card grading prices in November 2026: AGS $18 flat, CGC from $10, Beckett from $14.95, ISA $15, PSA from $24.99 and SGC a reported $50.

The fee is only part of the bill. Add shipping both ways, insurance and supplies, and at some graders a membership or a value upcharge. The table below uses each company's own listed prices as of November 18, 2026.

sections.note: Each company's own listed terms, checked November 18, 2026. Confirm before you ship.

p: Grading fees only, at each company's listed entry price. Shipping, insurance and supplies are extra everywhere.
list: AGS: $450 (30 x $15, bulk rate), 20 business days or less, subgrades included.
CGC Bulk: $300 if every card is worth $500 or less, 25 working days.
Beckett Base: $448.50, or $538.50 with subgrades, 45 business days or more.
PSA Value: $989.70, before any declared-value upcharge.

sections.h: What the fee does not cover
list: Shipping to the grader, tracked and insured.
Return shipping and insurance. AGS calculates it at checkout.
Supplies: penny sleeves, semi-rigid card savers, a box.
At some graders, a membership to reach the cheapest tier, a fee for subgrades, or a charge if the card is valued above the tier.

ranking.fit: Anyone with a mix of card values who does not want to pay by declared value.
ranking.lacks: Bulk pricing needs 30 cards. CGC's needs 10.
ranking.note: No value upcharge, no membership and no subgrade fee. Return shipping is added at checkout.

ranking.fit: Stacks of low-value cards: $10 each from 10 cards.
ranking.lacks: No measured report behind the grade.

ranking.fit: Modern card collectors who like the half-point scale.
ranking.lacks: Slow at the cheap tier. The fast tiers cost $80 to $125.

ranking.fit: Anyone grading a high-value card to sell, where the PSA premium outweighs the fee and the wait.
ranking.lacks: One grade, no subgrades, and fees that rise with declared value.

ranking.fit: Budget submitters who mainly want cards protected and labeled.
ranking.lacks: Little resale premium, and a 10 to 25 card minimum on every tier.

ranking.fit: Small sellers who would rather not choose a tier.
ranking.lacks: A small buyer pool. ISA slabs sell for less on most cards.

why: The price does not move with the card. AGS charges $18 per card whatever it is worth, with bulk tiers from $15 at 30 cards. PSA and SGC price by declared value and CGC caps each tier by card value, so a card that turns out to be worth more can cost more to grade.

Bulk pricing starts at 30 cards, a low bar for a dealer. TCG cards are $15 each at 20 business days, $20 at 10 and $30 at 5, and sports cards are $3 more per tier. Every card in a bulk order still gets the full report and eight subgrades.

You see why the card got its grade. AGS issues eight subgrades, four for the front and four for the back, plus a defect list and a 3D heightmap. Most graders hand back one number. A buyer who can open the report has less to argue about.

faq.q: What are the card grading prices?
faq.a: Most entry tiers cost $10 to $50 a card in November 2026. AGS is $18 with subgrades and a report included.

faq.q: Do graders charge more for valuable cards?
faq.a: Several do. PSA and SGC price by declared value, and CGC caps each tier by card value and moves a card up if it is worth more. AGS, Beckett, TAG and ISA say they add no upcharge for value.

faq.q: Is there a minimum number of cards?
faq.a: Not at AGS. You can send one card at $18, and bulk pricing needs 30. CGC's bulk tier needs 10 cards, ISA needs 10, and GMA needs 10 to 25 depending on the tier.

faq.q: How much does AGS charge to grade a card?
faq.a: $18 per card at the standard rate, whatever the card is worth. Bulk orders of 30 or more TCG cards are $15 each at 20 business days, $20 at 10 or $30 at 5. Sports and non-TCG bulk is $3 more per tier.

faq.q: Is it worth grading a low-value card?
faq.a: Only if grading lifts the price by more than the fee plus shipping, or if you want the card protected and documented. At $10 to $18 a card the math works on far more cards than at $50.
